samples.summary: Cursor invariant is healed in the paint path rather than on the store-change tick, so it is only true after a frame. `resolveCurrentSlide` is a read-shaped method that mutates `currentId`/`currentIndex`, cancels crop/text sessions, clears selection and fires `currentSlideListeners`, all from inside `render()`/`repaintOverlay()`. Other `store.onChange` subscribers (thumbnail-panel.ts:642, notes-panel.ts:80, keyboard.ts:573 nav) run before the RAF paint and can still observe the dangling id for that tick; docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md:241-246 places this kind of post-undo reconciliation on the notifyChange tick. Taste/layering, not a failed criterion.

Two divergent policies now exist for "where the cursor goes when the current slide is removed": the thumbnail panel's Delete action explicitly prefers the first survivor *after* the deleted run, while the new heal always lands on the slide *before* the vanished index. The panel's hand fixup is now largely redundant (the heal would cover it on the next frame), and whichever path wins gives a different landing slide for the same user gesture. Worth consolidating on one rule.

`currentIndex` is a second source of truth for the cursor that only `resolveCurrentSlide` maintains — `setCurrentSlide` (editor.ts:1491) and `setStore` (editor.ts:1605, which swaps in a `LayoutEditStore` with an unrelated slides array) assign `currentId` without updating it. It happens to be refreshed because both call `render()`, but the invariant is implicit; storing the index next to every cursor assignment (or deriving it) would make the pairing structural.

The new editor invariant ("currentId always names a slide the deck holds; removals heal to index-1") is recorded only in docs/tasks/active/*.md, not in any design doc. docs/design/slides/slides.md has no mention of the current-slide cursor and slides-native-undo.md's "Presence and selection" section describes only element-selection reconciliation. A one-line note folded into the canonical slides doc would keep the cursor policy discoverable alongside the thumbnail panel's rule. Not required for a bug fix.

Acceptance criterion "any removal of the current slide moves the cursor somewhere valid" is not satisfied for an empty deck: `resolveCurrentSlide` returns `undefined` and leaves the dangling `currentId` in place, so `getCurrentSlideId()` keeps naming a removed slide until something else assigns it. In practice deck-wipe is gated in the UI (thumbnail-panel.ts:301) and the documented behaviour says as much, so this is a documented gap rather than a real regression.
